Bank Glitch Sends ₹1 Lakh Crore Block Message to Rajasthan Employee During Recharge, Actual Balance ₹55,000

02 Nov 2026, 06:53 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.amarujala.com

2 min read

Key takeaways

Image: Amar Ujala · Photo source · Resized and letterboxed to 16:9; no AI generation

In this article
  1. Incident Overview
  2. Official Investigation and Resolution
  3. Practical Implications
  4. How to Verify the Original Announcement

Incident Overview

  • Sameer Khan, a medical store employee based in Sikar district of Rajasthan, received an SMS from his bank while attempting a mobile recharge.
  • The message claimed that ₹1 lakh crore had been blocked from his account, a sum that immediately raised alarm.
  • Simultaneously, his existing account balance of ₹55,000 was placed on hold, increasing his distress.
  • Khan shared the message with his employer and approached the local cyber police station to report the anomaly.

Official Investigation and Resolution

  • Assistant Sub-Inspector Dindayal of the Sikar cyber police verified the report and contacted the bank.
  • The investigation confirmed that the ₹1 lakh crore figure was never actualized; no such amount was deposited or blocked in Khan's account.
  • The bank acknowledged a technical glitch in its message-generation system as the root cause.
  • Following the bank's confirmation, the hold on the ₹55,000 balance was released, and Khan's account returned to its normal state.

Practical Implications

  • Erroneous SMS alerts, though uncommon, can cause unnecessary panic and temporary financial holds.
  • Customers are advised to verify account balances through official banking apps, websites, or ATMs rather than acting on suspicious messages alone.
  • Promptly contacting the bank’s customer care or visiting a branch can resolve such discrepancies swiftly.
  • Reporting such incidents to cyber police or the bank’s grievance cell helps in tracking and rectifying system errors.

How to Verify the Original Announcement

  • Check the current balance via the bank’s official mobile application or internet banking portal.
  • Visit a nearby ATM or use the bank’s missed-call balance inquiry service.
  • If the message appears dubious, refrain from making large transactions or transferring funds until the account status is confirmed.
  • For persistent concerns, lodge a formal complaint through the bank’s internal redressal mechanism or approach the RBI Ombudsman scheme.
